lens: Security — attack surface, OWASP class, DoS, data integrity, secrets, audit chain
answer: v5 delta introduces a settings-template kernel + filesystem-rendering adapter that becomes the canonical authority for what every account's per-provider settings (~/.claude/settings.json, ~/.codex/config.toml + hooks.json, ~/.gemini/settings.json) look like. From the F7 lens this expands attack surface in three material directions: (1) the renderer performs trust-following filesystem writes into $HOME with no stated symlink/TOCTOU defense ('atomic tempfile + rename(2)' is necessary but not sufficient — pre-positioned symlinks at the parent dir or merge-read step still escape the sandbox); (2) HookRef.command is a free-form String written into provider hook files that the CLIs subsequently exec()  on session events — without strict path-only validation this is a code-execution surface, and §B.2.1 ProviderOverrides.extra_hooks already documents a per-provider extension seam that touches this field; (3) the new AccountSnapshotProvider semantics extension silently excludes drifting accounts from snapshot() under VerifyMode::FailOnDrift with no audit-chain emission — only a runtime drift-report JSON is written, which is not the canonical audit chain at evidence/audit-chain.jsonl. Strong design points: SecretReference (sref://) is preserved end-to-end, env-var resolution happens at spawn-time NOT render-time, BLAKE3 file hashing for drift detection, atomic rename, CI-isolated render root under $CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR. But the security-critical gaps live in the boundary conditions: symlink handling, command-string validation, account_id path-component sanitization, hand-rolled TOML/JSON parser input-size caps, drift-report secret-leak surface (diff: Option<String> can echo a hand-edited settings file verbatim into a committed-state-dir artifact), case-sensitivity in provider/event string mapping, and the absent file-mode (chmod 0600) declaration on rendered files. severity_max: high, driven by the symlink + HookRef.command exec class. Secrets touched: true (sref:// throughout, OpenBaoAdapter wired). Tenant data touched: true (per-account MCP secret-ref bindings). Audit-chain emission required: true — CC-1 kernel_public_api change class mandates audit-chain rows for state-changing operations (every render writes to $HOME; every FailOnDrift exclusion changes a downstream selection set).
key_claims: v5 §B.3 declares 'Atomic: tempfile + rename(2)' for the writer, but the spec is silent on O_NOFOLLOW, symlink-checked open, and ownership/mode checks on the parent dirs (~/.claude, ~/.codex, ~/.gemini). rename(2) over a symlink replaces the link target, not the symlink itself, and §B.3 documents a 'merged with existing top-level keys' read-modify-write loop for Claude/Codex/Gemini which performs an UN-protected read of the existing settings.json (potentially attacker-controlled if the user dir was tampered with) — the merge bytes then flow into the new rendered output. This is a $HOME-rooted symlink-attack class.

v5 §B.2.1 HookRef { command: String, args: Vec<String> } is materialized into the provider hook files ~/.claude/settings.json:hooks[] and ~/.codex/hooks.json. The CLIs then exec() these commands when Stop/SessionStart/etc. events fire. The template TOML parser (v5.14 parse_template_toml, hand-rolled, no serde) has no declared validation that command is a path with no shell metacharacters, no whitespace ambiguity, and no NUL byte. Combined with §B.2.1 ProviderOverrides.extra_hooks (per-provider hook additions inside the same template), any future per-account overlay path that contributes extra_hooks injects code-execution into every Claude/Codex hook fire. RCE class at provider hook firing time.

v5 §B.4 specifies that VerifyMode::FailOnDrift causes the account to be 'excluded from the returned Vec<ProviderAccount>'. Downstream RoutePolicy::select (route-policy-kernel:54) cannot distinguish 'no account exists' from 'account was silently dropped for drift'. The drift outcome goes to .omc/state/settings-drift-report.json — that is a runtime state file, NOT the canonical evidence/audit-chain.jsonl audit chain (verified present, 13.6K, evidence/audit-chain.jsonl). Anti-pattern: missing-audit-chain-emission + silent-non-utf8-drop applied to account exclusion. For a CC-1 kernel_public_api change class, every state-changing operation on the AccountSnapshotProvider semantics extension must emit an audit-chain row.

v5 §B.5 CI lane constructs $CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR/settings-drift/<account_id>. AccountId is pub String (account-kernel:14-29) with no validation. account_id values like '../' or '/etc/passwd' or strings containing NUL would escape the CI sandbox. The plan does not declare a sanitizer at the path-join boundary. Same exposure for the production renderer if it ever joins account_id into a per-account state dir.

v5 §B.2.1 DriftEntry { state: DriftState, diff: Option<String> } says 'populated only for Modified'. The diff is emitted into the drift-report JSON (hand-rolled emit_drift_report_json, no serde). If a user hand-edited their ~/.claude/settings.json to put a literal secret in (e.g., a raw API key in mcpServers.*.env.AUTH instead of using sref://), the verify() pass reads that file and the diff field surfaces the literal bytes verbatim into .omc/state/settings-drift-report.json. C.29 acceptance row tests for no-raw-secrets in *rendered* output only — drift-report leakage is not gated. The .omc/state/ tree is observed in git status as a committed area (current branch has .omc/state/* tracked changes). Secret-in-evidence anti-pattern. Should redact or hash diff content.

v5 §B.7 v5.14 specifies 'hand-rolled TOML parser + JSON emitter (no serde)' for parse_template_toml and emit_drift_report_json. No documented maximum file size, depth limit, or array-length cap for input templates/foundry-supervisor/*.toml or registry/accounts/*.toml. Anti-pattern: unbounded-body-read on parser input. Hand-rolled parsers historically suffer quadratic-blowup and stack-overflow on malformed depth. C.27 only tests the Modified case; no parser-fuzz test is declared.

v5 §B.3 declares 'provider_family = "Claude"' (CamelCase) round-trips via ProviderFamily::try_from at account-kernel:40-50. v4 §B.0 already flagged that the string form is case-sensitive CamelCase ('OpenAIOrCodex' with capital AI). The new hand-rolled TOML parser must round-trip without normalization: a workspace author writing 'provider_family = "claude"' (lowercase) falls through try_from and is silently dropped or panics. Same hazard for HookEvent string parsing ('Stop' vs 'stop' vs 'STOP'). Anti-pattern: case-sensitive-header-lookup.

v5 §B.3 plus §B.2.1 ProviderOverrides do not declare a file-mode (chmod) for rendered output. Default umask on most workstations produces 0644 world-readable ~/.claude/settings.json. The file contains mcpServers.*.env entries whose VALUES are env-var NAMES (good) but whose KEYS reveal which secrets a workspace consumes — i.e., the topology of the workspace's secret store is leaked to every local UID. Rendered files holding tenant-config data should be 0600.

v5 §B.2.1 SettingsRendererError variants include Io(String), UnsupportedFormat(String), InvalidTemplate(String) — String payloads risk including raw filesystem paths and verbatim file content in error chains. If these errors are logged via tracing (workspace baseline at Cargo.toml:481-492), the raw paths and possibly raw bytes from the partially-parsed file land in logs. Anti-pattern: secret-in-log-line-or-evidence depending on what InvalidTemplate carries.

v5 §B.2.1 McpServerRef.env_secret_refs Vec<(String, SecretReference)> resolves at spawn-time (good); the kernel value type never holds raw bytes. SecretReference scheme validation (sref://) is at account-kernel:57-79 — verified existing. Renderer never serializes raw material. This is a load-bearing positive: the secret boundary is preserved end-to-end through the new kernel surface.

v5 §B.3 Codex case writes BOTH ~/.codex/config.toml (merged) AND ~/.codex/hooks.json (replaced wholly). The 'replaced wholly under a documented [foundry-supervisor] namespace' phrasing is contradictory — replaced-wholly means the foundry-supervisor namespace overwrites ANY existing user-authored hooks in that file. If a user has hand-installed non-foundry hooks under another section of hooks.json, those survive; if they accidentally placed them under foundry-supervisor, the renderer silently overwrites user-authored security hooks. Data-integrity class with low severity but worth a fence test.

v5 §B.6 R2 documents that GeminiRenderer reduces hooks to no-op until capability confirmed. That is honest, but it means workspaces that REQUIRE Stop-hook behavior for drain_response on a Gemini account effectively have NO drain hook — the supervisor's drain_response (v4 §B.4 step 14) silently degrades to whatever the v4 stop_hook_supported = false branch does. Capability-seed row mitigates this honestly, but no acceptance row checks the negative: that a Gemini account is correctly demoted or excluded when stop_hook_supported = false intersects with a workload that requires hooks.

v5 §C.29 acceptance test is well-designed: a known high-entropy fixture token is placed in OpenBao and the test asserts grep -RFq exits 1 (no match) on the rendered output. Additionally asserts every rendered mcpServers.*.env entry references an env-var name, never a literal value. This catches direct secret leakage at render-time. Recommend extending the same assertion to the .omc/state/settings-drift-report.json artifact (see finding above on diff field).

v5 §A.1.4 (b) Hook-event-mismatch pre-mortem maps HookEvent enum to provider event names via HookEventMap. The mapping is build-time tested via tests/hook_event_mapping.rs against captured fixtures. Good — but the mapping table itself is workspace-authored data; no integrity check (e.g., signature, hash pin) on the captured fixture files. A contributor mutating crates/oya-foundry-settings-template-adapter-fs/tests/fixtures/codex-hooks.observed.json could silently redirect Stop→PreToolUse mapping with no second signal. Recommend ADR-pinning the fixture hashes.

Surface attack-class delta is bounded by the kernel-public-API discipline: zero new public APIs on existing kernels (verified per §B.4 'SupervisorApp::new signature does NOT change'). The new attack surface is contained to two new crates and the templates/foundry-supervisor/ directory. lean-a10 (silent regression) is not triggered by this change in itself — but the silent account-drop in FailOnDrift mode IS a behavior-shift on the existing AccountSnapshotProvider port that ADR-foundry-settings-template-canonical-rendering should call out explicitly with a sunset-date for drift behavior toggling.
uncertainty_areas: Whether ~/.claude/settings.json (production target) has any pre-existing ownership or symlink hardening in the workspace boot flow — not visible from the plan. If a setup hook already validates that ~/.claude is owned by current UID and not a symlink, the symlink-attack severity drops from high to medium; if not, it remains high.

Whether per-account overlay (registry/accounts/<provider>.toml) is permitted to contribute HookRef.command or extra_hooks. Plan §B.2.1 ProviderOverrides.extra_hooks exists on the TEMPLATE side (workspace-controlled) but the per-account overlay flow path is not enumerated. If an attacker landing a registry/accounts/<provider>.toml row CAN contribute commands, RCE severity escalates; if only workspace-trusted templates can, severity is contained to insider-threat.

Whether .omc/state/settings-drift-report.json is gitignored or committed. Git status shows .omc/state/* IS tracked (last-tool-error.json, mission-state.json, hud-stdin-cache.json all modified in current working tree). If the drift-report is committed, the diff field becomes a persistent secret-leak vector. If gitignored, the leak window is local-only.

Whether HookEvent string parsing in the hand-rolled TOML parser uses byte-equal match or case-fold match — plan does not specify. ProviderFamily round-trip at account-kernel:40-50 is byte-equal (per v4 §B.0 verified). Consistent behavior would also be byte-equal but errors visibly rather than silently — needs verification at scaffold time.
Whether the workspace's tracing/log sink redacts InvalidTemplate(String) and Io(String) payloads. Cargo.toml:481-492 declares tracing as a baseline but no redaction layer is mentioned in v4/v5.

Whether the renderer enforces a maximum total file count or total byte count across all rendered outputs per account — relevant for the DoS class if a malformed template declares 10K [[hooks]] entries that each become a multi-KB JSON object.
Whether C.27's CI-isolated root mutation test runs as a non-root UID and whether $CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR is purged between runs — affects whether the test correctly exercises the merge-read path.

findings.summary: Renderer writes to ~/.claude/, ~/.codex/, ~/.gemini/ with no documented symlink defense. §B.3 specifies 'atomic tempfile + rename(2)' but is silent on O_NOFOLLOW, parent-dir ownership checks, and symlink-safe open for the merge-read step (Claude+Codex+Gemini all do read-modify-write of the existing settings file before writing). A pre-positioned symlink at ~/.claude/settings.json → /etc/passwd or ~/.claude → /tmp/attacker-dir/ causes the renderer to either read attacker-controlled bytes into the merge (poisoning the next rendered output) or write to an attacker-chosen path.
findings.recommended_action: Add to v5 §B.3 and the ADR an explicit Renderer Filesystem Trust Contract: (a) every parent dir on the target path must be opened with O_NOFOLLOW and stat-asserted to be a directory owned by the current UID with mode <= 0755; (b) the target file open must use O_NOFOLLOW|O_CLOEXEC and reject if the existing entry is a symlink; (c) the merge-read step must read from the same file descriptor that the rename will replace, not a fresh path-based open. Add acceptance row C.31: 'renderer refuses to write when target_path or any parent dir is a symlink'. Add F-RENDERER-SYMLINK-DEFENSE-1 to fixuptasks.

findings.summary: HookRef.command is a free-form String written into provider hook files (~/.claude/settings.json:hooks[].command and ~/.codex/hooks.json:[foundry-supervisor].hooks[].command) which the CLIs subsequently exec() on session events. The hand-rolled parse_template_toml has no declared rejection of shell metacharacters, embedded NULs, or relative paths. Combined with §B.2.1 ProviderOverrides.extra_hooks (per-provider hook extension seam in the template), any future per-account overlay path that contributes extra_hooks creates a code-execution surface fired by the provider at every Stop/SessionStart event.
findings.recommended_action: Add to §B.2.1 a HookCommandPath newtype with a constructor that rejects: any byte outside [a-zA-Z0-9_./\-$], any NUL, any '..' segment, any unescaped shell metacharacter ('$WORKSPACE_ROOT' must be the ONLY env-var prefix accepted and expanded by the renderer, not by the shell). The validator runs in the kernel (parse_template_toml emits InvalidTemplate on violation). Add acceptance row C.32: 'parse_template_toml rejects HookRef commands containing semicolons, backticks, command substitution, or relative paths'. Add F-HOOKREF-COMMAND-PATH-VALIDATOR-1.

findings.summary: VerifyMode::FailOnDrift silently excludes drifting accounts from AccountSnapshotProvider::snapshot() with no audit-chain emission. Downstream RoutePolicy::select cannot distinguish 'no account exists' from 'account dropped for drift'. Only a runtime .omc/state/settings-drift-report.json is written — that file is NOT the canonical audit chain at evidence/audit-chain.jsonl (verified present, 13.6K). For a CC-1 kernel_public_api change-class change that mutates AccountSnapshotProvider semantics, audit-chain emission is mandatory.
findings.recommended_action: Add to §B.4 and the ADR: every drift-driven account exclusion MUST emit an audit-chain row with shape { event: 'foundry_supervisor_settings_drift_exclude', change_id: 'M02-P06', account_id, provider_family, drift_states: [...], render_root_hash, timestamp }. Path: evidence/audit-chain.jsonl (append-only, hash-chained). Add acceptance row C.33: 'CI lane verifies one new audit-chain.jsonl row per excluded account in the FailOnDrift fixture'. The same applies to AutoReconcile mode — every render emits a 'foundry_supervisor_settings_render' row. Add F-DRIFT-EXCLUSION-AUDIT-EMISSION-1.

findings.summary: DriftEntry.diff: Option<String> is emitted into .omc/state/settings-drift-report.json via hand-rolled emit_drift_report_json. If a workspace user has hand-edited their ~/.claude/settings.json to include a literal secret (instead of using sref://), the verify() pass reads that file and the diff field carries the literal bytes verbatim into a state-tree artifact that — based on current git status showing .omc/state/* files tracked — is committed to the repository. C.29 acceptance gates rendered output for secrets but does NOT gate the drift-report artifact.
findings.recommended_action: (a) Either redact diff content (replace any value matching a configurable high-entropy regex with '<REDACTED-N-BYTES>'), OR (b) replace diff: Option<String> with diff_blake3: Option<[u8; 32]> + diff_byte_len: u64 so only a hash + size is leaked, OR (c) explicitly gitignore .omc/state/settings-drift-report.json AND add a pre-commit hook scanning that path. Recommendation: (b) — matches the BLAKE3 choice already in RenderManifest, and pairs cleanly with a side-channel local-only path for full diff content used only by interactive triage. Extend C.29 to also assert no high-entropy substring lands in settings-drift-report.json. Add F-DRIFTENTRY-DIFF-HASH-NOT-RAW-1.

findings.summary: $CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR/settings-drift/<account_id> in §B.5 concatenates account_id (pub String at account-kernel:14-29) into a filesystem path with no validation. account_id values containing '..', '/', or NUL escape the CI sandbox. Same pattern would apply to any future per-account state dir on the production side.
findings.recommended_action: Add to oya-foundry-account-kernel a path_component_safe(&self) -> bool method on AccountId (or a SafeAccountId newtype) that asserts ASCII alnum + '-' + '_' only, length <= 64. parse_template_toml and the CI subcommand both call this before joining. Reject malformed account_ids at the parse boundary, not at the path-join. Add acceptance row C.34: 'CI subcommand rejects an account_id containing ../ with a non-zero exit and an audit-chain row'. Add F-ACCOUNT-ID-PATH-SAFE-NEWTYPE-1.

findings.summary: Hand-rolled parse_template_toml and emit_drift_report_json (v5.14) declare no maximum input size, no nesting depth cap, no array-length limit. Unbounded-body-read class. A malformed or accidentally giant registry/accounts/*.toml or templates/foundry-supervisor/*.toml could OOM the verifier or exploit a quadratic-blowup in the hand-rolled parser. CI runner memory is not bounded by the plan.
findings.recommended_action: Declare in §B.7 v5.14 explicit caps: max_file_size_bytes = 1_048_576 (1 MiB) per .toml; max_array_len = 1024 per [[hooks]] / [[skills]] / [[mcp_servers]] / [[permissions]] / [[allowed_tools]]; max_nesting_depth = 8. Parser returns InvalidTemplate('exceeds size cap') early on any breach. Add fuzz target tests/parse_template_toml_fuzz.rs (cargo-fuzz not in Branch Y dep set — use hand-rolled corpus + random byte injection driven by std::time::Instant seed, mirroring §A.5 'no criterion' precedent). Acceptance row C.35: 'parse_template_toml rejects a 2 MiB synthetic template with InvalidTemplate'. Add F-TOML-PARSER-INPUT-CAPS-1.

findings.summary: ProviderFamily::try_from is case-sensitive CamelCase (verified v4 §B.0; 'Claude'/'OpenAIOrCodex'/'Gemini' exact). Hand-rolled HookEvent string parsing in the new TOML parser is unspecified for case handling. A workspace author writing 'provider_family = "claude"' or 'event = "stop"' silently falls through to either an error-panic or wrong-variant mapping, depending on parser implementation. Anti-pattern: case-sensitive-header-lookup combined with silent-drop.
findings.recommended_action: Specify in §B.2.1 and §B.3 that parse_template_toml performs a byte-equal match on provider_family and event values and emits InvalidTemplate with a precise expected-set on mismatch (no silent fallback, no case-fold normalization — round-trip integrity wins). Acceptance row C.36: 'parse_template_toml emits InvalidTemplate when event = "stop" (lowercase) or provider_family = "claude" (lowercase); the error message lists the accepted CamelCase set'. Add F-TOML-PARSER-CASE-STRICT-ERROR-1.

findings.summary: Plan does not specify file-mode (chmod) on rendered files. Default workstation umask produces 0644 on ~/.claude/settings.json containing mcpServers.*.env env-var-name bindings that reveal the workspace's secret-store topology to every local UID. Tenant-config data should not be world-readable.
findings.recommended_action: Specify in §B.3 that ClaudeRenderer/CodexRenderer/GeminiRenderer create rendered files with mode 0600 (owner read+write only). Use the tempfile + rename(2) sequence to also fchmod the tempfile before rename. Acceptance row C.37: 'cargo test::rendered_files_are_mode_0600 asserts every entry in RenderManifest.files has on-disk mode == 0o100600'. Add F-RENDERER-FILE-MODE-0600-1.

findings.summary: SettingsRendererError::Io(String), UnsupportedFormat(String), InvalidTemplate(String) carry free-form String payloads. If these flow into tracing-emitted log lines, raw filesystem paths and possibly raw partial-parse content land in logs. v4/v5 declare no log-redaction layer. Anti-pattern: secret-in-log-line-or-evidence (low because content in question is template/registry data, but template can carry sref:// strings which, while not literal secrets, do reveal vault layout).
findings.recommended_action: Add to §B.2.1 a Display impl on SettingsRendererError that redacts any sref:// substring to 'sref://<redacted>' and replaces home-rooted absolute paths with '~/<redacted-relative>'. Document in the kernel rustdoc that the Debug impl preserves full content for triage but Display is the only safe form for logging. Acceptance row C.38: 'cargo test::renderer_error_display_redacts_sref asserts no sref:// path leaks through Display'. Add F-RENDERER-ERROR-DISPLAY-REDACT-1.

findings.summary: v5 §A.1.4 (b) hook-event-mismatch mitigation pins HookEventMap to captured fixtures at crates/oya-foundry-settings-template-adapter-fs/tests/fixtures/{codex-hooks.observed.json, gemini-cli-help.observed.txt}. Plan does not declare a hash-pin or integrity check on these fixture files. A contributor mutating the fixture could silently redirect HookEvent::Stop → some other provider event with no second signal — the affected supervisor would then never receive Stop and drain_response would silently never fire.
findings.recommended_action: Add to ADR-foundry-settings-template-canonical-rendering a fixture-hash-pin clause: the fixture filenames and their BLAKE3 hashes are committed into registry/capabilities/foundry-supervisor.toml (mirrors the v4 §B.5 capability-seed file pattern). CI lane lean-settings-drift verifies the fixture hash matches before invoking HookEventMap mapping. Acceptance row C.39: 'fixture-hash mismatch fails the lane with a precise diff'. Add F-HOOKEVENTMAP-FIXTURE-HASH-PIN-1.

findings.summary: GeminiRenderer reduces hooks to no-op per §B.6 R2 (capability-seed hooks_supported = false). This is honest, but no acceptance row verifies the NEGATIVE: that the supervisor correctly demotes or excludes a Gemini account when a workload requires hooks (e.g., drain_response). v4 step 14 documents the stop_hook_supported = false branch but v5 does not extend a test to the cross-product of (Gemini account, hook-required workload).
findings.recommended_action: Add acceptance row C.40: 'integration test::gemini_no_hooks_account_demoted_when_workload_requires_drain_hook asserts the SupervisorVerdict for a Gemini account on a hook-requiring workload is DemoteAndRetry { new_tier: <one-below-current>, reason: contains "hooks_supported=false" }'. Path: crates/oya-foundry-supervisor-app/tests/gemini_no_hooks.rs. Add F-GEMINI-NO-HOOKS-DEMOTION-TEST-1.

remediation_priority_order: F-RENDERER-SYMLINK-DEFENSE-1 (HIGH — exploitable by pre-positioned $HOME symlink; full RCE/data-exfil class)
F-HOOKREF-COMMAND-PATH-VALIDATOR-1 (HIGH — RCE class at provider hook fire; mitigates per-account overlay seam)
F-DRIFT-EXCLUSION-AUDIT-EMISSION-1 (HIGH — CC-1 mandates audit-chain on state-changing semantics extension)
F-DRIFTENTRY-DIFF-HASH-NOT-RAW-1 (MEDIUM — secret-in-evidence on committed state-tree artifact)
F-ACCOUNT-ID-PATH-SAFE-NEWTYPE-1 (MEDIUM — CI sandbox escape + future production state-dir hazard)
F-TOML-PARSER-INPUT-CAPS-1 (MEDIUM — unbounded-body-read DoS on hand-rolled parser)
F-RENDERER-FILE-MODE-0600-1 (MEDIUM — vault-topology leak to local UIDs)
F-RENDERER-ERROR-DISPLAY-REDACT-1 (LOW — sref:// path leak via logs)
owasp_secondary_classes: broken_access (A01) — PermissionEntry.rule and AllowedTool.name pass through verbatim with no syntax validation; if any future per-account overlay extends permissions, blanket 'Bash(*)' rules could be injected; F1_linus already flagged these as zero-info newtypes
injection (A03) — HookRef.command (covered by F-HOOKREF-COMMAND-PATH-VALIDATOR-1); CRLF injection class in hand-rolled JSON emitter for drift-report
logging (A09) — silent-drop on FailOnDrift (covered by F-DRIFT-EXCLUSION-AUDIT-EMISSION-1)
component_vuln (A06) — Branch Y commitment means zero new external deps; positive — narrow attack surface from dependency churn
